harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed inventory-worker as a systemd-managed background service on node1, confined via NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, and ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory (plus additional hardening: PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, empty capability bounding set, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, etc). Verified via nsenter into the running service's namespaces that writes to /etc fail (read-only filesystem) while writes to /var/lib/inventory succeed, and confirmed NoNewPrivs=1 in /proc/<pid>/status. Completed the mandatory single-node restart on node1: captured pre-restart boot_id and service health baseline, issued systemctl reboot, polled until reconnect, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the service auto-started (enabled), resumed appending to the same persisted log file with a new PID, and retained identical sandbox confinement post-restart.
actions_performed: Created system user 'inventory' (nologin) and set ownership (inventory:inventory, mode 750) on /var/lib/inventory
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh: a long-running loop appending heartbeat lines to /var/lib/inventory/inventory.log

Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service running as User=inventory with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, plus ProtectHome, PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, ProtectKernelTunables/Modules/Logs, ProtectControlGroups, ProtectClock, ProtectHostname, RestrictSUIDSGID, RestrictRealtime, RestrictNamespaces, LockPersonality, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, RemoveIPC, empty CapabilityBoundingSet/AmbientCapabilities, UMask=0027
Enabled and started the service; confirmed active/enabled state and continuous log growth
Falsified confinement via nsenter into the service's mount namespace: write to /etc failed with 'Read-only file system', write to /var/lib/inventory succeeded; confirmed NoNewPrivs=1
Captured pre-restart boot_id (4d340bf4-...) and service health baseline
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 (sole managed node) via backgrounded exec so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified boot_id changed to 548db637-... confirming a real restart
Verified inventory-worker.service auto-started (enabled=yes) with new PID 924 and resumed appending to the same inventory.log
Re-ran the /etc read-only vs /var/lib/inventory writable nsenter test post-restart to confirm sandboxing persisted

evidence.requirement: Service created and running, confined to /var/lib/inventory with no new privileges
evidence.summary: Created inventory user/dir, worker script, and systemd unit with NoNewPrivileges/ProtectSystem=strict/ReadWritePaths; service shown active and writing heartbeats to /var/lib/inventory/inventory.log

evidence.requirement: Proof that confinement actually restricts writes outside /var/lib/inventory and blocks privilege escalation
evidence.summary: nsenter into running service's namespaces: write to /etc failed (read-only filesystem), write to /var/lib/inventory succeeded, NoNewPrivs=1 confirmed

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before restart (boot identity + service health)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 4d340bf4-0579-47f0-98c1-5c17a66d50f1, service active/enabled, and growing log tail prior to reboot
systemctl reboot issued in background; exec stream closed as node went down, confirming the reboot command was accepted

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Polling attempts failed while node was down (timeout, connection reset), then succeeded with new boot_id 548db637-5b42-455e-9d6a-911d67c75f73, differing from the pre-restart value

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of service and data, and persistence of sandbox confinement
evidence.summary: Service auto-started (enabled=yes) with new PID 924, resumed appending to the same inventory.log file; nsenter re-test confirmed /etc still read-only and /var/lib/inventory still writable with NoNewPrivs=1 after restart
